t: Gyeongju was the capital of Silla from the kingdom's traditional founding in 57 BCE until its surrender in 935, and after the unification of the peninsula up to the Taedong River in 668 it was the centre of Korean political and cultural life.
Under Goryeo and Joseon it lost its national standing, though it kept a place as a regional centre until the provincial capital passed to Daegu in 1601.
Many of its buildings and sculptures were damaged by invasions and by Neo-Confucian radicals, and the tombs and Buddhist sites that survive are the main record of the Silla city.
dyk: The name Sŏrabŏl, by which Gyeongju was known in the Silla period, eventually evolved into a Korean word for a capital city, as in Seoul.
ev: Saro-guk, the later Silla, is established when six villages unite under Bak Hyeokgeose
The unification of the peninsula up to the Taedong River makes Gyeongju the centre of Korean political and cultural life
King Gyeongsun surrenders his title and country to Taejo of Goryeo
King Taejo gives the city the name Gyeongju
Gyeongju is designated the Eastern Capital of Goryeo, a title removed in 1012
The provincial capital passes to Daegu
A museum, the forerunner of the Gyeongju National Museum, opens to show the finds from the excavated tombs
The city of Gyeongju is united with the surrounding county

f.founded: According to Korean records, probably based on the dynastic chronicles of Silla, the state of Saro-guk was established in 57 BCE when six small villages in the Gyeongju area united under Bak Hyeokgeose, the first ruler of Silla.
f.where: On the banks of the Hyeongsan River in the Gyeongju Basin, in the far south-eastern corner of North Gyeongsang Province in South Korea, with the Sea of Japan to the east.
f.known: Capital of Silla; Sŏrabŏl; the Silla court and its tombs; Bulguksa and Seokguram; the Cheomseongdae observatory; the Hwarang; Gukhak, the national academy of 682; birthplace of Cheondoism
f.today: Gyeongju is a city of North Gyeongsang Province in South Korea, an urban and rural complex formed in 1995 when the city and the surrounding county were united.
